checks.source_anchors: v3 Section6 Remarks6.1-6.3, Lemma6.4, Proposition6.5 and Theorem6.8; source1231-1338
checks.reason: The actual section permits free H and strongly inert rank-two subgroups of its whole Magnus subgroup. For H=F(a,b),A=H,B=<a^2,b^2>, substitution is injective and B is proper infinite index by abelianization and Schreier. All iterated images have rank2, so s_Z=infinity. The ascending Bass-Serre tree has one backwards edge and infinitely many forwards choices; every finite directed segment has the terminal vertex stabilizer, a rank-two conjugate of H. Continuum many directed biinfinite lines through H exist, whereas H and G are countable. Hence continuum many H-orbits and uncountably many non-axes contradict both universal conclusions.
checks.counterevidence: Finite-length orbit bounds can still hold; identifying elements need not be compatible as segment length increases. The standard t-axis does satisfy the needed condition, so the weaker existence conclusion used by Theorem6.8 is not refuted. The final one-relator main theorem is not declared false.
checks.repair_check: A new proof of periodic-line existence in the needed class is required; deleting universal wording alone does not repair the dependency through Theorem6.8/Corollary6.9.

checks.reason: The noncompact pentagonal strip has trivial vertex and edge groups, hyperbolic quasi-line vertex space, and free Bass-Serre-line action. Both spanning-tree normal forms are prefix closed and relative, since A/B are subtrees and common tails cancel; every omitted edge has length4 detour, yielding uniform quasigeodesics. The induced same-strip form has length2^m, while the explicit m-step upward/zero-index downward path has length4m+1. It meets the stated three hypotheses but no common quasigeodesic bound.
checks.counterevidence: The finite X/Z application in Theorem5.9 is compact and is not refuted.
